errorKind.tool-limit: The provider refused the request because it carries too many tools. The catalog already trims the least used families on the next attempt — resend the message.
errorKind.moderation: The provider blocked this response with its content filter. This runs on the provider's servers and can't be turned off from here — it misfires often on turns that include images. Switching to another model resolves it.
errorKind.model-unavailable: This provider doesn't serve the selected model. Pick another model to continue.
errorKind.rate-limit: The provider hit its usage or request limit. Wait a bit or switch models.
errorKind.network: Network error talking to the provider (timeout, outage). Try again or switch models.
errorKind.context-length: The conversation grew past the model's context window, so the provider refused the request. Switching models won't help — compact the conversation (the button on the context meter, or /compact) or start a new one.
errorKind.context-length-turn: The work in this reply (tool results piling up across many steps) outgrew the model's context window, so the provider refused the next request. The conversation itself still fits, so compacting won't help: send a message asking it to continue — the new reply starts without this one's tool results.

analytics.hoursByProjectInfo: The total estimates the combined working time (Orbit + you), not raw clock time. Orbit's generation time always counts. Your breaks enter with an inactivity margin: up to 30 min count in full (reading, testing or reviewing); 30–60 min count in full if you return with a detailed message; 1–1.5 h count only half, and only with a very long message. tip.text: All modes and their settings are available in the message input. Use the toggles below the input to turn them on/off quickly, or click the "+" button to access Subagents, Orchestra, and Loop with their advanced settings.

modes.label: Research
modes.description: Searches and reads web pages via HTTP.
modes.detail: Adds the websearch and webfetch tools to the agent. Fast and efficient for looking up documentation, APIs, and public information. Doesn't run JavaScript — ideal for static content.

modes.label: Browser
modes.description: Navigates pages like a real browser.
modes.detail: Opens the right panel with a full browser. Runs JavaScript, ideal for SPAs, forms, and dynamic pages. The agent can navigate, click, fill fields, and take screenshots.

modes.label: Thinking
modes.detail: Enables the model's reasoning/thinking mode (when supported). The model "thinks" before answering, resulting in deeper, better-grounded replies. Uses more tokens and time.

modes.label: Simple
modes.detail: Removes advanced formatting, citations, and tool blocks from the response. Useful when you just want the essential content, no frills.

modes.label: Memory (Brain)
modes.description: Orbit remembers facts and preferences across conversations.
modes.detail: Adds the memory_save/search/link/open/graph tools. Orbit can save facts, preferences, and decisions and automatically retrieve them in future conversations. Turn it off per chat if you prefer a context-free interaction.

modes.label: Subagents
modes.description: Ephemeral background workers for parallel tasks.
modes.detail: Adds the subagent tool to the agent. When it spots independent subtasks, it can delegate them to ephemeral workers running in the background with the configured model. Those workers are discarded when the task ends — they never appear in the sidebar. In Orchestra mode this toggle is also what lets the orchestrator delegate research while planning: without it, it investigates the project itself by reading files.

modes.label: Orchestra
modes.description: Plans and splits work across persistent workers — when the request calls for it.
modes.detail: The orchestrator first decides what the request is: a simple question it answers right away (and may offer "want me to implement it?"), an ambiguity that would change the split it asks about, and only real work becomes a plan. While planning it reads the project and registers the subtasks, with dependencies when order matters (tests after the feature, for example), and proposes the plan for your approval. Each task becomes a persistent child session, in code mode, running with the worker model — up to 4 at a time. In the gear you choose how it behaves after splitting: Orchestrate only (runs and synthesizes), Follow along (reviews each worker as it finishes, looking at the diff, asks for adjustments and creates extra workers, within the adjustments-per-worker limit) or Strict (also runs the project's checks before accepting). You can also isolate each worker in its own worktree and let the orchestrator merge everything at the end. In later messages it still sees the conversation's workers and can continue one of them instead of creating another.

modes.label: Loop
modes.description: The agent reviews and iterates until the task is complete.
modes.detail: After each answer, the result is critically reviewed. If the goal wasn't reached, the agent keeps going on its own in a new iteration, with what's missing spelled out. The only setting is the maximum number of iterations (in the gear) — a ceiling, not a target: the loop stops as soon as the review says it's done. It doesn't apply to the Orchestra: there, the orchestrator does the reviewing.

modes.label: Plan Mode
modes.description: Read-only — produces a plan without editing files.
modes.detail: Blocks write tools (write, edit, bash). The agent only reads the code and produces a detailed implementation plan. Useful for review and planning before making changes.

modes.label: Permissions
modes.description: Security control over the agent's actions.
modes.detail: Three levels: Ask (asks before each critical action), Approve (shows a summary for approval), Full (executes automatically). Configurable in the Preferences modal or directly in the input.

modes.label: Vision
modes.description: Delegates vision to a dedicated model.
modes.detail: With the mode on, images (screenshots and attachments) are described by a configured vision model and only the text description enters the agent's context — never the raw image. Beneficial even for models with native vision: in long conversations, the image isn't reloaded into the context every turn, saving tokens and keeping the context lean.

combos.label: Deep research
combos.description: Turn on Research + Browser + Thinking together. The agent searches, navigates complex pages, and reasons deeply about what it found. Ideal for investigating technical topics, comparing documentation, or doing competitive analysis.

combos.label: Automatic refinement
combos.description: Loop + Thinking: the agent reviews its own result with extended reasoning, spotting gaps and refining until the goal is achieved. Great for generating robust code, thorough tests, or detailed documentation.

combos.label: Workers on multiple fronts
combos.description: Orchestra + Subagents: unlocks delegation at both levels. While planning, the orchestrator may call subagents to research before splitting (without the toggle it reads the project itself). And it can hand a worker its own subagents when a task is too broad for one.

combos.label: Careful planning
combos.description: Plan Mode + Thinking + Research: before any change, the agent researches documentation, reasons deeply, and produces a detailed implementation plan without modifying files. Approve the plan, then execute it with the normal tools.

combos.label: Safe coding
combos.description: Ask permission + Loop: on each loop iteration, the agent can ask for permission before sensitive actions (editing files, running commands). Safe for reviewing third-party code or making changes in production.

prerequisites.title: Prerequisites
prerequisites.hint: Whatever is off, the agent says it cannot do instead of making it up.

master.title: Control the computer
master.description: Enables the tools that read the screen and the accessibility tree of apps and act on them. Even when on, it only applies to conversations where you turn on the Computer mode.

pointer.title: Pointer
pointer.description: Directed sends clicks and keys straight to the app without touching your cursor. Global uses the real pointer: it moves the cursor and is the only one that can drag.

edge.title: Screenshot size
edge.description: Longest side of the image sent to the model. Larger = more detail and more tokens.

permissions.title: macOS permissions
permissions.description: Accessibility reads apps and sends clicks and keys; Screen Recording takes the screenshots.
permissions.dev: In development the permission belongs to this project's "Electron" binary — other Electron projects show up with the same name in Settings and don't count. Use "Request" to create the right entry. Screen Recording needs an app restart.
permissions.responsible: Orbit was launched by {{app}}, so macOS checks the permissions on {{app}} — not on "Electron" or "Orbit". Allow {{app}} in Accessibility and Screen Recording, or open the app from Finder. Screen Recording needs a restart.
permissions.screenManual: If Orbit doesn't show up in the Screen Recording list, macOS didn't add it on its own: click the + below the list, pick Orbit in Applications, turn it on and restart Orbit.

test.title: Test
test.description: Does a real read of the frontmost app — confirms the permission applies to the process that does the work.

safety.title: Safety
safety.description: Password managers, System Settings and security prompts are blocked. The agent never types into password fields. Each app (and each site, in browsers) asks for approval in the conversation, and {{shortcut}} stops everything at once.

windows.title: Windows
windows.description: Windows asks for no permission. Orbit uses UI Automation through a PowerShell that stays open in the background.
windows.ready: Ready: the UI Automation host is working.
windows.down: The UI Automation host did not start: {{reason}}
windows.elevated: Apps running as administrator cannot be controlled by Orbit; neither can the UAC prompt or the lock screen.

unavailable.but: Unavailable in the Mac App Store version: the store sandbox blocks accessibility and event posting. Use the version from the website.
unavailable.platform: For now, available on macOS and Windows only.

model.title: Computer agent model
model.hint: Multi-step tasks in other apps go to a dedicated agent with a short context. Without a model here it uses the auxiliary model (when it supports tools), otherwise the conversation's — and moves up to the conversation's model only when it gets stuck. It reads screens as text, so vision is not required.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.description: Your own commands that run on their own before or after each of the agent's tools, without going through the model. Exit 2 blocks the call (before) or sends stderr back to the agent (after).

form.timeoutHint: If it runs longer, the command is stopped and the call goes on without it. Default 10, max 60.
form.commandHintPre: Receives the call as JSON on stdin and the vars ORBIT_TOOL_NAME, ORBIT_FILE and ORBIT_PROJECT_DIR. Exit 2 blocks and stderr becomes the reason.
form.commandHintPost: Receives the call and its result as JSON on stdin and the vars ORBIT_TOOL_NAME, ORBIT_FILE and ORBIT_PROJECT_DIR. Exit 2 sends stderr back to the agent.

mcp.title: Ask Orbit for an MCP server
mcp.description: Say which service or tool you want to connect. The model sets up the configuration (command or URL) and you fill in the keys and review it in the next step.
mcp.placeholder:
E.g.: connect the GitHub MCP server so the agent can read issues and pull requests.

Or: a local files server restricted to the ~/Documents folder.
mcp.review: Suggested by Orbit. Replace the values between < > with your keys and check the command before saving.

skills.title: Ask Orbit for a skill
skills.description: Describe what the skill should teach the agent and when to use it. The model writes the name, description and instructions — you review everything in the next step.
skills.placeholder:
E.g.: a skill to review pull requests my way: check tests, naming and security risks, and answer in short bullets with what blocks the merge.

Or: a skill that writes commit messages as type(scope): sentence.
skills.review: Suggested by Orbit. Review the name, description and instructions before saving.

hooks.title: Ask Orbit for a hook
hooks.description: Say what should happen on its own around the agent's tools. The model writes the command — you check it in the next step.
hooks.placeholder:
E.g.: every time the agent edits a TypeScript file, run prettier on it.

Or: block any git push --force before it runs.
hooks.review: Suggested by Orbit. The command runs on its own on your machine, so check it before saving. Everything is editable.

agents.title: Ask Orbit for an agent
agents.description: Say what the agent is for and how it should work. The model writes the name, the "when to use" line and the prompt — you review everything in the next step.
agents.placeholder:
E.g.: an agent that reviews contracts: points out risky clauses, never edits files, answers in short bullets.

Or: a Motion agent for 10-second logo stings with a clean, minimal style.
agents.review: Suggested by Orbit. Read the prompt before saving: it speaks to the model with system authority.
